blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Retrieval-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) models enable efficient test-time adaptation by leveraging expert demonstrations as additional context without updating model parameters. However, even when retrieved demonstrations are relevant to the current task, the VLA may fail to effectively utilize the retrieved information, ultimately leading to task failure. To address this challenge, we propose R2-VLA, a risk-controlled retrieval-augmented VLA framework that enables reliable test-time adaptation by satisfying a user-specified task success rate requirement with minimal expert assistance. Specifically, R2-VLA learns an uncertainty predictor that estimates the uncertainty of the VLA's predicted actions given the retrieved demonstrations, guiding when to act autonomously or request expert assistance. We further introduce a task-level risk-control procedure that calibrates the uncertainty threshold to satisfy a user-specified task-failure risk requirement. Moreover, R2-VLA continually incorporates expert corrections into its retrieval memory to improve future adaptation while preserving the prescribed task-level risk guarantee. Experiments across three VLA backbones and four LIBERO benchmark suites demonstrate that R2-VLA improves average task success by 9.2--11.2 percentage points, achieving the desired target with fewer expert requests. These results highlight the effectiveness of connecting the usefulness of retrieved demonstrations with task-level risk control to enable successful robotic manipulation.
blocks.zh: 检索增强的视觉-语言-行动(VLA)模型在不更新模型参数的情况下,通过利用专家演示作为额外背景,使测试时间能够有效适应。 然而,即使检索到的演示与目前的任务相关,志愿军可能无法有效利用检索到的信息,最终导致任务失败. 为了应对这一挑战,我们提议使用R2-VLA,这是一个风险可控的检索增强VLA框架,通过满足用户指定的任务成功率要求,在最低限度的专家协助下,实现可靠的测试时间适应。 具体来说,R2-VLA学会了一种不确定性预测器,在检索到的演示中估计VLA预测行动的不确定性,指导何时自主行动或请求专家援助。 我们还采用了任务一级风险控制程序,对不确定性阈值进行校准,以满足用户指定的任务失败风险要求。 此外,R2-VLA继续将专家更正纳入其检索内存,以改进今后的适应工作,同时保留规定的任务级别风险保障。 跨越三个甚高频主干线和四个LIBERO基准套件的实验表明,R2-VLA将平均任务成功率提高了9.2-11.2个百分点,在专家请求较少的情况下实现了预期目标. 这些结果突出表明了将检索演示的效用与任务一级的风险控制联系起来,以便能够成功地进行机器人操纵的有效性。

blocks.en: Recent advances in vision-language-action (VLA) models [ 7 , 22 , 32 , 38 , 8 , 9 , 40 , 37 ] have enabled a single policy to perform a broad range of robotic manipulation tasks, highlighting their potential as general-purpose robotic control policies. However, even strong pre-trained VLAs often require substantial fine-tuning or retraining to maintain reliable performance under distribution shifts, such as new environments, unseen objects, or novel task instructions [ 45 ] , limiting their ability to rapidly adapt at deployment time. In contrast, Large Language Models (LLMs) can adapt to new tasks at inference time through in-context learning (ICL): given only a small number of input-output demonstrations as context, an LLM can adjust its behavior without updating its model parameters [ 10 , 15 , 28 ] . Inspired by this paradigm, recent work such as RICL [ 36 ] introduces in-context adaptation to pre-trained VLAs. Specifically, RICL maintains a compact retrieval buffer of expert demonstrations and, at each decision step, retrieves demonstrations relevant to the current observation as additional context for the VLA policy, enabling effective adaptation to previously unseen deployment conditions without parameter updates.
blocks.zh: 视觉语言动作模型[7,22,32,38,8,9,40,37]的近期进步,使得单一政策能够执行广泛的机器人操纵任务,突出了其作为通用机器人控制政策的潜力. 然而,即使是经过预先训练的强力VLA也往往需要进行实质性的微调或再培训,以在分配的转变下保持可靠的性能,例如新的环境,看不见的物体,或者新的任务指示[45],限制他们在部署时迅速适应的能力. 相比之下,大语言模型(LLMs)可以通过内文本学习(ICL)在推论时适应新任务:由于作为上下文的输入输出演示数量很少,一个LLM可以不更新其模型参数而调整其行为[10,15,28]. 受这一范式的启发,RICL[36]等近期作品引入了对预训VLA的内在适应. 具体地说,区域国际法中心维持着专家示范的紧凑检索缓冲器,并在每一决定步骤中,检索与当前观察有关的示范,作为志愿军政策的额外背景,以便能够在不更新参数的情况下,有效地适应先前未见的部署条件。

blocks.en: The effectiveness of retrieval-based in-context adaptation depends critically on which demonstrations are retrieved, since these examples determine what task-specific information is provided to the VLA at deployment. Prior work [ 36 , 45 ] , including RICL, relies on visual similarity between the current observation and observations in the retrieval buffer to select relevant demonstrations. Recent approaches have explored improved retrieval mechanisms [ 21 , 44 , 25 ] , such as incorporating task instructions and learning embeddings that better capture behavioral relevance. However, improving retrieval quality does not necessarily guarantee successful task execution [ 26 ] . Even when the retrieved demonstrations are relevant to the current task, the VLA may still fail to translate the retrieved information into appropriate actions for its current state. As illustrated in Fig. 1 (a), RICL retrieves behaviorally relevant demonstrations but nevertheless moves the bowl in the wrong direction, ultimately leading to task failure. This suggests the usefulness of retrieved demonstrations depends not solely on their relevance to the current task, but ultimately on whether they enable the VLA to successfully complete it.
blocks.zh: 以检索为基础的内在文字适应的有效性关键取决于哪些演示材料被检索,因为这些例子决定了部署时向志愿军提供哪些具体任务的信息。 先前的作品[36,45],包括RICL,依赖于当前观测和检索缓冲器中的观测之间的视觉相似性来选择相关的演示. 最近的办法探讨了改进的检索机制[21、44、25],例如纳入任务指示和学习嵌入,以更好地反映行为的相关性。 然而,提高检索质量并不一定保证任务的成功执行[26]. 即使检索到的演示与当前任务相关,志愿军仍然可能无法将检索到的信息转化为适合其目前状况的适当行动。 如图1(a)所示,RICL检索与行为相关的演示,但将碗移向错误方向,最终导致任务失败。 这表明检索到的演示是否有用不仅取决于其与当前任务的相关性,而且最终取决于它们是否使志愿军成功完成.

blocks.en: In this work, we propose R2-VLA , a risk-controlled retrieval-augmented VLA framework that enables reliable test-time adaptation by satisfying a user-specified task success rate. As discussed above, retrieving relevant demonstrations alone is insufficient for successful task execution, as the VLA may still fail to effectively utilize the retrieved information. Therefore, R2-VLA enables the VLA to determine when it can act autonomously and when additional assistance is necessary to successfully complete the task. To this end, we augment the VLA with a learned uncertainty predictor that estimates how uncertain the VLA is about its predicted actions, given the current observation, retrieved demonstrations, and its own prior knowledge. When the predicted uncertainty is below a specified threshold, the VLA executes its own action autonomously ( Act ). Otherwise, it requests expert assistance ( Ask ) to avoid potentially incorrect actions, as illustrated in Fig. 1 (b). However, determining an appropriate uncertainty threshold is nontrivial, as the predicted uncertainty does not directly correspond to task-level success. We therefore introduce a risk-control procedure that calibrates the threshold to satisfy a user-specified task-failure risk requirement. In this way, R2-VLA directly connects the usefulness of retrieved demonstrations to their ability to support successful task completion.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们提出R2-VLA,这是一个风险可控的检索增强VLA框架,通过满足用户指定的任务成功率,能够进行可靠的测试时间调整。 如上所述,仅仅检索有关演示不足以成功执行任务,因为志愿军可能仍无法有效利用所检索的信息。 因此,R2-VLA使VLA能够确定何时可以自主行动,何时需要额外援助才能成功完成任务. 为此,我们用一个有学问的不确定性预测器来增强志愿军,该预测器估计,鉴于目前的观察、检索的演示以及自己先前的知识,志愿军对其预期行动有多不确定。 当预测的不确定性低于规定的阈值时,VLA自行执行行动(Act.). 否则,如图1(b)所示,它请求专家协助(询问)以避免可能不正确的行动。 然而,确定适当的不确定性阈值是非三角性的,因为预测的不确定性并不直接对应任务一级的成功。 因此,我们采用了一种风险控制程序,对门槛进行校准,以满足用户指定的任务失败风险要求。 这样,R2-VLA直接将检索演示的有用性与其支持成功完成任务的能力联系起来.

blocks.en: To summarize, our contributions are as follows: 1. We propose R2-VLA , a risk-controlled retrieval-augmented VLA framework that learns to estimate the uncertainty of its predicted actions given retrieved demonstrations and determines when to Act or Ask to satisfy a user-specified task-level failure risk requirement. 2. We theoretically establish a connection between uncertainty prediction accuracy and task-level failure risk (Theorem 1 ). We further extend R2-VLA to continual adaptation by incorporating expert corrections into the retrieval buffer and theoretically establish that the prescribed task-level risk can be preserved throughout adaptation (Theorem 2 ). 3. We conduct extensive experiments across three VLA backbones and four LIBERO benchmark suites, demonstrating consistent improvements of 9.2 9.2 – 11.2 11.2 percentage points in average task success over RICL, while meeting the desired target in most settings with minimal expert assistance.
blocks.zh: 概括而言,我们的贡献如下: 1. 我们提议使用R2-VLA,这是一个风险可控检索增强的VLA框架,它学会估计其预测行动的不确定性,提供检索的演示,并确定何时采取行动或要求满足用户指定的任务一级故障风险要求。 2. 我们理论上确定不确定性预测准确性和任务一级故障风险之间的联系(定理1)。 我们进一步将R2-VLA扩大到持续适应,将专家更正纳入检索缓冲,并在理论上确定,在整个适应过程中可以保留规定的任务级别风险(定理2)。 3. 我们在三个VLA主干线和四个LIBERO基准套件上进行了广泛的试验,显示平均任务比RICL成功9.29.2 - 11.2 11.2个百分点的不断改进,同时在多数情况下,在专家协助最少的情况下达到预期目标。

blocks.en: Even behaviorally relevant demonstrations do not necessarily enable a retrieval-augmented VLA to complete a task successfully. We therefore propose R2-VLA , which determines when the VLA can act autonomously and when it should request expert assistance, with the goal of satisfying a user-specified task success requirement while minimizing the frequency of expert assistance. We first formulate the R2-VLA policy (Section 3.1 ), then describe how the uncertainty predictor is learned (Section 3.2 ) and how its threshold is calibrated using task outcomes (Section 3.3 ). Finally, we introduce continual deployment adaptation (Section 3.4 ) and present the theoretical results (Section 3.5 ).
blocks.zh: 即使与行为相关的演示也不一定能使一个检索增强的VLA成功完成任务. 因此,我们提议R2-VLA,它确定志愿军何时可以自主行动,何时应请求专家协助,目的是满足用户指定的任务成功要求,同时尽量减少专家协助的频率。 我们首先制定R2-VLA政策(第3.1节),然后说明如何学习不确定性预测器(第3.2节),如何利用任务结果校准其阈值(第3.3节)。 最后,我们提出持续部署适应(第3.4节),并介绍理论结果(第3.5节)。

blocks.zh: 3.2 学习不确定性预测器

blocks.en: As discussed above, the uncertainty predictor provides a per-step signal to guide Act / Ask decisions by assessing the VLA’s uncertainty about its predicted action from its internal representations, rather than relying on external retrieval quality metrics, such as the DINO distance used by RICL. We characterize action uncertainty through the discrepancy between the VLA’s predicted action and the corresponding expert action, where a large discrepancy indicates that the VLA’s predicted action deviates from the desired expert behavior, potentially leading to task failure. We therefore train the uncertainty predictor to estimate this discrepancy, as detailed below.

blocks.en: A key challenge is ensuring that the uncertainty head learns failure modes specifically induced by retrieval. If it is trained only with ordinary retrieval contexts from 𝒟 ret \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}} , most retrieved demonstrations may be helpful, providing relatively few examples in which retrieval actively degrades the resulting action. We therefore augment uncertainty-head training with deliberately degraded retrieval contexts, including wrong-task retrieval, visually similar retrieval associated with a different goal, and random or uninformative retrieval, as detailed in Appendix 8.3 Table 3 . Crucially, these corrupted contexts are used to teach the uncertainty head action uncertainty , rather than retrieval abnormality. A poor or unusual retrieval should not necessarily result in high uncertainty if the VLA can still produce the correct action from its pretrained knowledge. In this case, u t ≈ 0 u_{t}\approx 0 , and the desired uncertainty remains small. Conversely, a retrieved context may appear behavior relevant while steering the VLA toward an incorrect behavior, in which case u t ≫ 0 u_{t}\gg 0 and the uncertainty should be correspondingly large. We provide an ablation study on the effect of incorporating corrupted retrieval contexts during uncertainty-head training in Appendix 9.2 , Table 6 .

To solve the threshold selection problem in Eq. ( 1 ), we adopt the risk-control framework introduced in Sec. 2 to identify thresholds that satisfy the prescribed task-failure risk requirement with high probability and select the one with the lowest empirical ASK rate among the certified candidates. Specifically, since the deployment distribution 𝒫 \mathcal{P} is unknown, we construct a held-out calibration set 𝒟 cal = { Z i } i = 1 N cal \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{cal}}=\{Z_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N_{\mathrm{cal}}} to empirically estimate the population risk R ⁡ ( λ ) R(\lambda) and ASK rate H ⁡ ( λ ) H(\lambda) . The calibration set consists of independent task instances sampled from 𝒫 \mathcal{P} and is disjoint from the data used for retrieval and uncertainty learning. Each task instance Z i = ( ξ i , l i text ) Z_{i}=(\xi_{i},l_{i}^{\mathrm{text}}) specifies an initial environment configuration and task instruction. blocks.en: The risk-control procedure in Sec. 3.3 calibrates the threshold λ ^ \hat{\lambda} for a fixed retrieval buffer 𝒟 ret \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}} . During deployment, however, every Ask decision provides new expert experience at states where the current retrieval memory is insufficient. We therefore use these expert corrections to continually expand the retrieval buffer and improve future adaptation as summarized in Algorithm 2 . Formally, we organize deployment into adaptation rounds indexed by q = 0 , 1 , … , Q q=0,1,\ldots,Q . In practice, a new adaptation round can be triggered after a fixed number of deployment rollouts. At the beginning of round q q , R2-VLA uses a fixed retrieval buffer 𝒟 ret ( q ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q)} together with its calibrated threshold λ ^ ( q ) \hat{\lambda}^{(q)} (Algorithm 2 , Line 1). Throughout the round, R2-VLA follows the Act / Ask decision rule (Algorithm 2 , Lines 5–8). Whenever Ask is triggered, the external expert provides a corrective action a t E a_{t}^{\mathrm{E}} for the current input x t x_{t} . All corrections collected during round q q are stored in a temporary correction buffer ℬ corr ( q ) = { ( x m , a m E ) } m = 1 N corr ( q ) \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{corr}}^{(q)}=\{(x_{m},a_{m}^{\mathrm{E}})\}_{m=1}^{N_{\mathrm{corr}}^{(q)}} (Algorithm 2 , Line 8). At the end of the round, these corrections are incorporated into the retrieval memory as 𝒟 ret ( q + 1 ) = 𝒟 ret ( q ) ∪ ℬ corr ( q ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q+1)}=\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q)}\cup\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{corr}}^{(q)} (Algorithm 2 , Line 11). Notice that updating the retrieval buffer changes the behavior of the R2-VLA policy, even though the model parameters remain frozen. For the same query x t x_{t} , the updated memory 𝒟 ret ( q + 1 ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q+1)} may return a different retrieved context than 𝒟 ret ( q ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q)} , thereby changing both the predicted action a ^ t \hat{a}_{t} and its uncertainty u ^ t \hat{u}_{t} . Consequently, the previously calibrated threshold λ ^ ( q ) \hat{\lambda}^{(q)} is not guaranteed to preserve the target task-failure rate after the memory update. We therefore recalibrate the threshold after each memory update. Specifically, after constructing 𝒟 ret ( q + 1 ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q+1)} , we draw a fresh calibration set 𝒟 cal ( q + 1 ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{cal}}^{(q+1)} and rerun the risk-control procedure in Algorithm 1 using the updated retrieval buffer (Algorithm 2 , Line 12). This produces a new certified threshold λ ^ ( q + 1 ) \hat{\lambda}^{(q+1)} , which is then used throughout the next adaptation round.

The proof is provided in Appendix 7.1 . Theorem 1 decomposes the task-failure risk into several interpretable components. The first term represents the failure probability of the expert policy, while the second term arises from the numerical stabilization constant η \eta and becomes negligible when η \eta is sufficiently small. The remaining two terms characterize the contribution of the learned uncertainty signal to task-level success rate. Specifically, the third term measures the cumulative predicted uncertainty over autonomously executed actions, indicating that task-failure risk can be reduced when the robot acts autonomously primarily in low-uncertainty states. The final term captures uncertainty prediction error through the uncertainty-regression loss ℒ U ​ ( λ ) \mathcal{L}_{U}(\lambda) , highlighting the importance of accurately predicting action discrepancy, particularly avoiding severe underestimation of large action errors. Together, these results provide theoretical motivation for learning an accurate uncertainty predictor and using it to determine when the VLA can act autonomously and when expert assistance is necessary. blocks.en: We implement R2-VLA policy following the model architecture adopted in RICL [ 36 ] , which uses π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST as the VLA backbone. To evaluate the generality of our method across different model architectures and scales, we additionally consider MiniVLA [ 5 ] and OpenVLA [ 22 ] as smaller- and larger-scale VLA models, respectively. We evaluate R2-VLA on LIBERO [ 24 ] , a simulated robotic manipulation benchmark based on the Franka Panda arm. LIBERO contains four suites designed to evaluate different forms of manipulation generalization: Spatial , Object , Goal , and Long . For each suite, we use 20 expert demonstrations per task to construct the retrieval buffer and maintain a disjoint set of 20 demonstrations per task for risk calibration. During evaluation, when Ask is triggered, a separately trained expert policy provides the action for the current observation. We report task success over 100 evaluation rollouts per task using a held-out evaluation set that is disjoint from both the retrieval and calibration buffers. In addition to task success rate, we report the ASK rate, denoted by H ^ ​ ( λ ) \widehat{H}(\lambda) as defined in Section 3.3 , which measures the fraction of decision points at which R2-VLA requests expert assistance. Additional implementation details are provided in Appendix 8 . Additional ablation studies investigating the effects of the target risk level ϵ \epsilon , retrieval corruption during uncertainty-head training, and calibration-set size N cal N_{\mathrm{cal}} are provided in Appendix 9.2 .

blocks.en: Table 1 reports the task success rates and ASK rate of R2-VLA compared with RICL. R2-VLA consistently improves task success over the corresponding RICL baseline across all backbone–task suite combinations, demonstrating the effectiveness of identifying uncertain retrieval-guided behaviors and requesting expert assistance. Moreover, R2-VLA generally achieves the prescribed task-level success targets, which are typically set at least 5 5 percentage points above the corresponding RICL baseline. Specifically, R2-VLA reaches or exceeds the target success rate in 11 of the 12 settings. The only exception is π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST on LIBERO- Object , where the achieved success rate of 78.9 % 78.9\% is slightly below the 80.0 % 80.0\% target. This small diviation may be due to limited number of evaluation rollouts, as our risk-control guarantee in Theorem 2 is statistical rather than a deterministic guarantee on every evaluation set. The ASK rate further reflect the varying difficulty of successful execution across task suites. In particular, LIBERO- Long , which exhibits the lowest success rate across all three backbones, also requires the highest ASK rate. In contrast, the other suites generally require fewer expert assistance while still achieving their prescribed success targets. These results suggest that R2-VLA can adapt its reliance on expert assistance to the uncertain of predicted execution across different tasks and VLA architectures.

blocks.en: Improved task success alone does not establish that the learned uncertainty identifies decision points where retrieved demonstrations are insufficient for successful VLA execution, as task success may also improve simply by delegating more actions to an expert. We therefore compare R2-VLA against a Random ASK baseline that requests expert assistance at randomly selected decision points while matching the expert assistance frequency of our method. This comparison isolates the benefit of identifying uncertain retrieval-guided behaviors rather than merely increasing expert involvement. To further investigate whether learning action uncertainty from the VLA is necessary, we consider two alternative uncertainty signals: (1) DINO Distance , which uses the visual feature distance employed by RICL for demonstration retrieval as its uncertainty score, and (2) Action Entropy , which instead estimates uncertainty from the VLA’s action distribution. The DINO Distance variant directly evaluates whether the original retrieval quality metric is sufficient to identify when retrieved demonstrations provide insufficient behavioral guidance, while the Action Entropy variant evaluates whether the model’s predictive uncertainty can identify uncertain actions without training an additional uncertainty estimator. For these two baselines, thresholds are independently calibrated using the same risk-control procedure as R2-VLA, allowing us to compare the resulting trade-offs between task success and ASK rate. We additionally report the average action discrepancy during ACT, defined as 𝔼 ⁡ [ ∑ t = 1 T 𝕀 ⁡ { ACT t } ​ u ^ t ] 𝔼 ⁡ [ ∑ t = 1 T 𝕀 ⁡ { ACT t } ] \frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{I}\{\mathrm{ACT}_{t}\}\hat{u}_{t}\right]}{\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{I}\{\mathrm{ACT}_{t}\}\right]} . This metric provides empirical support for the mechanism highlighted in Theorem 1 by evaluating whether R2-VLA effectively prevents actions with large expert discrepancies from being executed autonomously.

blocks.en: Table 2 shows that R2-VLA outperforms all three baselines. Specifically, under the same ASK budget, Random ASK achieves an average success rate that is 6.5 6.5 percentage points lower than R2-VLA. This demonstrates that the improvement cannot be attributed solely to additional expert assistance. Instead, selectively identifying decision points where retrieval-guided behaviors are uncertain is critical for successful task execution. Compared with DINO Distance, R2-VLA achieves higher task success while requiring fewer expert assistance. This indicates that retrieval quality metrics alone are insufficient to determine whether the retrieved demonstrations enable the VLA to successfully complete the task, as illustrated in Fig. 1 (a). Similarly, R2-VLA outperforms Action Entropy, suggesting that uncertainty derived directly from the action distribution is less effective than our learned uncertainty predictor. Notably, R2-VLA achieves a more favorable empirical trade-off between task success and ASK rate than both DINO Distance and Action Entropy. Moreover, R2-VLA achieves the lowest ACT error across all four LIBERO suites. This further supports Theorem 1 , showing that the learned uncertainty effectively identifies actions for autonomous execution, thereby contributing to lower task-level failure risk. Overall, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of learning action uncertainty from retrieval-augmented VLA representations. Complete results for other VLA backbones are provided in Appendix 9.1 Table 5 .

blocks.en: We next evaluate whether expert corrections collected through Ask can improve future task success while reducing the need for external assistance. Following Algorithm 2 , we divide deployment into adaptation rounds. During each round, the retrieval buffer and calibrated threshold λ ^ \hat{\lambda} remain fixed, and expert corrections are collected whenever the robot requests assistance. At the end of each round, these corrections are incorporated into the retrieval memory, followed by recalibration using Algorithm 1 . Specifically, we execute fresh calibration using the updated retrieval memory as detailed in Appendix 8.1 , ensuring that calibration satisfies the requirement of Theorem 2 . For consistent comparison across rounds, we evaluate each updated policy on the same held-out evaluation sets as before. We maintain the same fixed target success rate as in Table 1 .
blocks.zh: 我们接下来评估通过Ask收集的专家更正能否改进今后任务的成功,同时减少对外部援助的需求。 根据算法2,我们把部署分为适应回合。 在每一回合中,回收缓冲和校准阈值 ^ ^ ^ \ lt\lambda } 保持不变,每当机器人请求协助时,都会收集专家更正. 在每回合结束时,这些校正都纳入检索内存,然后使用算法重新校正 1 (英语). 具体来说,我们使用附录8.1详述的更新的检索内存进行新校准,确保校准符合定理2的要求。 为了对各轮工作进行一致的比较,我们评价每项最新政策,评价内容与以往相同。 我们保持与表1相同的固定目标成功率。

blocks.en: Figure 2 illustrates the evolution of R2-VLA using the π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST backbone across memory adaptation rounds. As expert corrections are progressively incorporated into the retrieval memory, task success consistently improves while the frequency of expert assistance decreases. Importantly, after the initial memory update, the observed success rates meet or exceed the prescribed targets across adaptation rounds, providing empirical evidence consistent with Theorem 2 . Meanwhile, the decreasing ASK rate suggests that accumulated expert corrections provide increasingly useful retrieval experiences, enabling the VLA to achieve higher task success with less external assistance. We further examine how the calibrated threshold λ ^ \hat{\lambda} evolves as the retrieval memory grows. As shown in Figure 2 , the threshold varies across adaptation rounds, with distinct patterns across task suites. These changes reflect the evolving distribution of uncertainty scores induced by updates to the retrieval memory, which can alter both the retrieved demonstrations and the resulting action predictions. Therefore, a threshold calibrated for an earlier retrieval buffer may no longer provide the desired risk control after memory updates. By recalibrating λ ^ \hat{\lambda} after each adaptation round, R2-VLA adjusts its ACT/ASK decisions to the updated policy. The results also show that this recalibration can be performed with relatively modest computational overhead, with calibration wall time remaining approximately stable across later adaptation rounds. Together, these findings demonstrate that R2-VLA can progressively improve autonomous task execution and reduce expert dependence while empirically maintaining the prescribed task-level success rate requirement.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: In this work, we proposed R2-VLA, a risk-controlled retrieval-augmented VLA framework that enables reliable test-time adaptation by satisfying a user-specified task success rate requirement with minimal expert assistance. R2-VLA learns an uncertainty predictor to determine when to act autonomously and when to request expert assistance. We further introduced a risk-control procedure that calibrates the uncertainty threshold to satisfy the prescribed task-level failure risk requirement. Moreover, R2-VLA supports continual adaptation by incorporating expert corrections into retrieval memory and preserving task-level risk control. Experiments across various settings demonstrate consistent improvements in task success over RICL while requiring less frequent expert assistance. Overall, our work represents a step toward building more reliable and adaptive robotic systems that can recognize their own limitations, seek assistance when necessary, and continually improve through interaction with their environments.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们提出了R2-VLA,这是一个风险可控的检索增强VLA框架,通过满足用户指定的任务成功率要求,在最低限度的专家协助下,能够进行可靠的测试时间调整。 R2-VLA学习了不确定预测器,以确定何时自主行动,何时请求专家援助. 我们还采用了一种风险控制程序,对不确定性阈值进行校准,以满足规定的任务一级故障风险要求。 此外,R2-VLA通过将专家更正纳入检索内存和维护任务一级的风险控制,支持持续调整。 各种环境的试验表明,在任务成功方面,区域技术中心不断改进,同时需要较少的专家援助。 总体而言,我们的工作是朝着建设更可靠和适应性更强的机器人系统迈出的一步,这些系统能够认识到自身的局限性,在必要时寻求援助,并通过与环境的互动不断改进。

blocks.en: 6 Related Work
blocks.zh: 6 相关工作

blocks.en: Retrieval-Augmented VLA. While recent vision-language-action (VLA) models, such as OpenVLA [ 22 ] and π 0 \pi_{0} [ 7 ] , have demonstrated strong generalization through pretraining on large and diverse robot datasets, adapting them to new tasks often still requires task-specific fine-tuning or retraining, limiting their ability to behave as truly generalist agents. In contrast, humans can rapidly adapt to novel tasks by drawing on prior experience [ 3 , 34 , 39 ] . Motivated by this capability, recent work has explored in-context imitation learning, in which demonstrations of a new task are provided directly to the VLA at inference time, enabling adaptation without updating the model parameters. ICRT [ 17 ] is an early representative approach, formulating robot control as next-token prediction over sequences of visual observations, proprioceptive states, and actions. By placing one or more human teleoperation trajectories in the transformer’s context, ICRT can infer and execute previously unseen tasks without test-time parameter updates, demonstrating that the in-context learning behavior of autoregressive models can extend from language to continuous robotic control. More recently, RICL [ 36 ] showed that such capability does not naturally emerge in pretrained VLAs and proposed explicitly post-training a pretrained π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST policy to exploit retrieved demonstrations. At deployment, RICL retrieves relevant states and actions from a small demonstration buffer and incorporates them into the model context, enabling adaptation to new manipulation tasks using roughly 10–20 demonstrations without updating model parameters.
blocks.zh: 检索-获得VLA. 虽然近期的视觉语言动作(VLA)模型,如OpenVLA[22]和π0\pi_{0}[7],通过对大型和多样的机器人数据集进行预训,显示出强烈的概括性,使其适应新的任务,往往仍然需要针对特定任务进行微调或再培训,限制其作为真正概括性代理人的行为能力. 相比之下,人类可以通过借鉴以往的经验[3,34,39]迅速适应新任务. 以这种能力为动力,最近的工作探索了文字仿真学习,其中在推论时间直接向VLA演示一项新任务,使得能够在不更新模型参数的情况下进行适应. ICRT[17]是一种早期的代表性方法,将机器人控制作为下一个对视觉观测,自主状态,和行动等序列的预测. 通过在变压器的上下文中放置一个或多个人类电传操作轨迹,ICRT可以在没有测试时间参数更新的情况下推断并执行之前未见的任务,表明自递式模型的内文本学习行为可以从语言扩展到持续的机器人控制. 最近,RICL [36] 表明这种能力不会自然地出现在经过预先训练的志愿军中,并明确提出经过预先训练的 0\pi_{0}-FAST政策来利用收回的示威。 在部署时,RICL从一个小型演示缓冲器中检索相关的状态和行动,并将其纳入模型背景,从而能够在不更新模型参数的情况下,利用大约10-20个演示来适应新的操纵任务。

blocks.en: A parallel direction investigates whether existing frozen VLAs can benefit from demonstrations without additional in-context learning (ICL) training. Retrieval-VLA [ 45 ] enables training-free adaptation by identifying relevant past experiences and directly incorporating the retrieved information into the predictions of a frozen VLA. Since the VLA does not need to learn how to interpret retrieved demonstrations as in-context examples, this approach avoids ICL-specific post-training. Similarly, ReCAP [ 31 ] extends VLA policies to new tasks by conditioning on demonstrations from an external retrieval pool without task-specific retraining. Beyond directly leveraging retrieved demonstrations, recent methods further explore how to improve their relevance and utilization. StellaVLA [ 43 ] converts retrieved trajectories into structured task plans, subgoals, and motion descriptions to provide richer task-specific guidance. RA-VLA [ 21 ] introduces behavior-aligned retrieval and grounded execution to improve the relevance of retrieved demonstrations, while ICI-VLA [ 44 ] employs spatiotemporally aligned demonstrations to better match the current task phase and geometry. Collectively, these studies demonstrate the potential of retrieval-based adaptation for extending VLA capabilities without task-specific parameter updates. Building on these advances, our work addresses the complementary challenge of ensuring successful task execution given retrieved demonstrations by introducing uncertainty-guided expert assistance and task-level risk control.
blocks.zh: 一个平行的方向是调查现有的被冻结的VLA是否能够从示威中获益而不进行额外的内文学习(ICL)培训. 检索-VLA[45]通过查明过去的相关经验,并将检索到的信息直接纳入冻结的VLA的预测中,实现了无培训适应。 由于VLA不需要学习如何将检索到的演示解释为内容内的例子,这种方法避免了ICL特定的后培训. 同样,ReCAP[31]将VLA政策扩大到新的任务,在不进行特定任务再培训的情况下,以外部检索库的演示为条件。 除了直接利用检索到的演示之外,最近的方法还进一步探讨了如何提高这些演示的相关性和利用。 StellaVLA [43] 将检索的轨迹转换为结构化的任务计划,子目标和运动描述,以提供更丰富的特定任务指导. RA-VLA [21] 引入行为对齐的检索和有根据的执行,以提高被检索的演示的相关性,而ICI-VLA [44] 则采用瞬间对齐的演示,以更好地匹配当前的任务阶段和几何. 这些研究集体表明,基于检索的适应有可能在不更新特定任务参数的情况下扩展VLA能力。 在这些进展的基础上,我们的工作通过引入以不确定性指导的专家援助和任务层面的风险控制,解决确保成功完成任务这一补充挑战。

blocks.en: Uncertainty in Robotics. Uncertainty has long been used in robot learning to determine when autonomous execution of the robot should be deferred to an expert [ 13 , 20 , 29 , 46 ] . Early confidence-based learning-from-demonstration methods allow a robot to request demonstrations in states where its learned policy is insufficiently confident [ 13 ] . This principle was later incorporated into interactive imitation learning. EnsembleDAgger [ 29 ] uses ensemble disagreement to determine when a learned policy can safely act [ 29 ] . More recently, ConformalDAgger [ 46 ] replaces heuristic uncertainty thresholds with online conformal calibration, enabling uncertainty estimates to adapt under deployment-time expert shift.
blocks.zh: 机器人学的不确定性 在机器人学习中长期使用不确定性来确定何时自主执行机器人应推迟到专家[13,20,29,46]. 早期基于信心的学习-从演示方法允许机器人请求在其学到的政策缺乏足够信心的州进行演示[13]. 这一原则后来被纳入交互式模仿学习中. EnsembleDagger [29] 使用综艺分歧来决定一个学到的政策何时可以安全行动 [29]. 最近,ConformalDagger[46] 以在线一致性校准取代了热力不确定性阈值,使不确定性估计数能够在部署时间专家转移时进行调整。

blocks.en: Recent work has extended uncertainty estimation to VLA models. SAFE [ 19 ] estimates uncertainty from the internal representations of a VLA to assess the reliability of ongoing task execution and determine when intervention may be needed. ReconVLA [ 11 ] uses conformalized action uncertainty to compare candidate actions and select the least uncertain action for execution. [ 35 ] estimate epistemic uncertainty in flow-based VLAs to identify unreliable predictions and prioritize informative samples for active adaptation. SCALE [ 14 ] uses self-uncertainty to adapt both visual perception and action generation, encouraging broader exploration under high uncertainty and more confident execution under low uncertainty. [ 18 ] use calibrated uncertainty to gate control among normal VLA execution, pause-and-reobservation, and fallback planning. Collectively, these methods demonstrate the value of uncertainty estimation for identifying potentially incorrect robot actions and determining when expert assistance is necessary. Building on these advances, our work introduces task-level risk control to calibrate the uncertainty threshold, enabling the VLA to satisfy a user-specified task success requirement while minimizing the frequency of expert assistance.
blocks.zh: 最近的工作将不确定性估计扩大到了VLA模型。 安全局[19] 估计一个志愿军内部代表的不确定性,以评估正在进行的任务执行的可靠性并确定何时可能需要干预。 ResconVLA [11] 使用统一动作不确定性来比较候选动作,并选择最不不确定动作来执行. [35] 估计流基VLA的概论不确定性,以确定不可靠的预测,并确定信息化样本的优先顺序,以便积极适应. SCALE [14] 使用自我不确定性来适应视觉感知和动作生成,鼓励在高度不确定性下进行更广泛的探索,在低不确定性下进行更自信的执行. [18] 在正常的VLA执行中,使用校准的不确定性来控制闸门,暂停和反观察,以及倒置规划. 这些方法共同表明不确定性估计对于确定可能不正确的机器人行动和确定何时需要专家援助的价值。 在这些进展的基础上,我们的工作引入了任务层面的风险控制,以校准不确定性阈值,使志愿军能够满足用户指定的任务成功要求,同时尽量减少专家援助的频率。

blocks.en: Risk Control for Robotics. Statistical risk-control techniques [ 4 , 2 , 1 ] have recently been applied to LLM-based robotic planning. KnowNo [ 33 ] uses conformal prediction to construct sets of candidate robot actions, executing autonomously when the prediction set is sufficiently unambiguous and otherwise requesting human assistance. Introspective Planning [ 23 ] improves the underlying LLM reasoning before conformal calibration to reduce unnecessary clarification while retaining statistical success guarantees. [ 41 ] extends conformal planning to multi-robot systems. [ 42 ] propose conformal-aware finetuning to reduce prediction-set size and human-help rates. In contrast, we study risk control for VLAs during closed-loop task execution. Rather than calibrating the uncertainty of an individual action, we calibrate the uncertainty threshold that determines when the VLA acts autonomously and when it requests expert assistance. The threshold is evaluated through complete task rollouts, so the resulting risk criterion directly reflects whether the induced VLA policy succeeds or fails at the task level. This formulation also accounts for the sequential nature of VLA execution, where locally uncertain decisions can affect subsequent states and ultimately determine task success.
blocks.zh: 机器人的风险控制。 统计风险控制技术[4、2、1]最近已应用于基于LLM的机器人规划。 Know No [33] 使用一致的预测来构建一组候选机器人动作,在预测足够明确或以其他方式请求人力援助时自主执行. 内观规划[23]改进了基础的LLM推理,然后进行校准,以减少不必要的澄清,同时保留统计成功保障. [41] 将符合性规划扩展至多机器人系统。 [42] 提出符合感知的微调,以降低预测设定的大小和人力-帮助率. 相比之下,我们研究了在闭路任务执行期间对甚高频控制的风险。 我们不是调整个别行动的不确定性,而是调整确定志愿军何时自主行动以及何时要求专家援助的不确定性门槛。 阈值通过完全的任务展开来评价,因此由此产生的风险标准直接反映了被引领的VLA政策在任务层面上的成败. 这种提法还考虑到志愿军执行的顺序性质,当地不确定的决定可能会影响以后的状态,并最终决定任务的成功.

blocks.en: Assumption 1 is a standard smoothness condition for continuous-control systems. It requires the environment dynamics to vary continuously with the executed action. If two action chunks are close, then the corresponding next-state distributions are also close. Similar Lipschitz-type assumptions on transition dynamics are commonly used in reinforcement learning [ 6 , 12 , 27 ] .

blocks.en: Theorem 2 establishes that continual growth of the retrieval memory does not invalidate the task-risk control. The retrieval buffer 𝒟 ret ( q ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q)} at round q q may depend arbitrarily on all previous robot trajectories, uncertainty values, Ask decisions, and expert corrections. The key requirement is that, once this updated retrieval buffer is fixed, the threshold is recalibrated using a fresh set of calibration episodes. This distinction is important because adding expert corrections changes the retrieval-augmented policy itself. For the same state x t x_{t} , the updated buffer may produce a different retrieved context, action prediction, and uncertainty score. Consequently, a threshold calibrated for 𝒟 ret ( q ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q)} need not remain valid after the memory is updated to 𝒟 ret ( q + 1 ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{ret}}^{(q+1)} . Our round-wise recalibration procedure explicitly accounts for this change.

blocks.en: 8.1 Benchmark and Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: 8.1 基准和评价议定书

blocks.en: We evaluate R2-VLA on LIBERO [ 24 ] , a simulated robotic manipulation benchmark based on the Franka Panda arm. Each demonstration contains multi-view visual observations, including front-view and wrist-view images, together with proprioceptive states, natural-language task instructions, and expert actions. We consider all four LIBERO suites: Spatial , Object , Goal , and Long , which evaluate different aspects of manipulation generalization. For each suite, we partition the available demonstrations into disjoint sets for retrieval and policy adaptation, risk calibration, and evaluation. Specifically, demonstration IDs 10 10 – 29 29 are used to construct the retrieval buffer, perform suite-specific RICL adaptation, and train the uncertainty head, corresponding to 20 demonstrations per task and 200 demonstrations per suite. Demonstration IDs 30 30 – 49 49 are reserved for risk calibration, while IDs 0 0 – 9 9 are held out for evaluation and are not used for policy adaptation, uncertainty-head training, or risk calibration.
blocks.zh: 我们评价R2-VLA在LiBERO上[24],一个基于Franka Panda臂的模拟机器人操纵基准. 每个演示都包含多视图视觉观察,包括前视图和腕景图像,以及自控状态,自然语言任务说明,以及专家行动. 我们考虑所有四个LIBERO套房:空间、对象、目标、Long, 对于每个套房,我们把现有的演示分为回收和政策调整、风险校准和评价的脱节套件。 具体来说,示范ID 10 10– 29 用于构建检索缓冲器,进行特定套件的RICL改造,并训练不确定头,相当于每个任务20个演示和每套200个演示. 示范ID 30 – 49 49 用于风险校准,而ID 0 – 9 9 用于评估,不用于政策调整,不确定性头培训,或风险校准.

blocks.en: During deployment, whenever R2-VLA selects Ask , a separately trained expert policy provides the corrective action for the current observation. The expert policy is trained using demonstration IDs 0 0 – 49 49 for each suite and serves exclusively as an action oracle without updating the evaluated VLA during execution. We report task success and ASK rates over 100 evaluation rollouts per task.

blocks.en: For risk calibration, we construct a predefined candidate threshold set Λ = { λ 1 , … , λ K } \Lambda=\{\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{K}\} with K = 10 K=10 . Specifically, we first collect uncertainty scores from five preliminary rollouts using demonstration IDs 30 30 – 34 34 . Let 𝒰 ref = ⋃ i = 1 5 { u i , t } t = 1 T i \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ref}}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{5}\{u_{i,t}\}_{t=1}^{T_{i}} denote the pooled uncertainty scores across these rollouts, where T i T_{i} is the number of decision steps in rollout i i . We compute the reference threshold as λ ref = Quantile 0.60 ⁡ ( 𝒰 ref ) . \lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}=\operatorname{Quantile}_{0.60}\left(\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ref}}\right). We then construct Λ \Lambda by selecting K = 10 K=10 candidate thresholds evenly spaced over the interval [ λ ref − 0.1 , λ ref + 0.1 ] [\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}-0.1,\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}+0.1] . The resulting candidate set is fixed before applying the risk-control procedure in Algorithm 1 .

To evaluate continual memory adaptation, we organize deployment into successive adaptation rounds following Algorithm 2 . Within each round, the retrieval buffer and calibrated threshold remain fixed, and expert corrections are collected whenever R2-VLA requests assistance. At the end of each round, these corrections are incorporated into the retrieval memory, followed by threshold recalibration using Algorithm 1 . Specifically, demonstration IDs 30 30 – 49 49 remain designated for calibration, while fresh initial states are independently sampled from the task initialization distribution at each round. We then perform new calibration rollouts using the updated retrieval memory to obtain the calibrated threshold for the next round.

To evaluate whether R2-VLA generalizes across different VLA architectures and model scales, we additionally consider MiniVLA [ 5 ] and OpenVLA [ 22 ] . Across all three backbones, four retrieved demonstrations are provided as in-context examples for each query, i.e., M = 4 M=4 . Training exclusively on clean retrieval contexts provides limited supervision for states in which retrieval is misleading. We therefore augment the training data with deliberately corrupted retrieval contexts. These corruptions are designed to expose the uncertainty head to situations in which the retrieved examples may appear plausible but provide incorrect or uninformative guidance for the current action. blocks.en: 9.1 Expert Assistance Strategies Baselines on MiniVLA and OpenVLA.
blocks.zh: 9.1 微型和轻型飞行器及开放VLA专家援助战略基线。

blocks.en: We evaluate the effectiveness of different expert assistance strategies on MiniVLA and OpenVLA, with the complete results reported in Table 5 . Consistent with the findings for π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST in the main paper, R2-VLA achieves the highest average task success rate while requiring substantially fewer expert assistance than alternative uncertainty-based strategies. Specifically, on MiniVLA, R2-VLA achieves an average success rate of 62.8% with an ASK rate of only 20.8%, outperforming DINO Distance (58.5% success with 34.0% ASK) and Action Entropy (58.8% success with 34.0% ASK). Similarly, on OpenVLA, R2-VLA achieves 68.6% success with 33.3% ASK, compared with 66.8% success and 51.4% ASK for DINO Distance, and 67.3% success and 51.6% ASK for Action Entropy. These results demonstrate that the learned uncertainty identifies more informative decision points, allowing R2-VLA to achieve higher task success with less expert assistance.
blocks.zh: 我们评价关于MiniVLA和OpenVLA的不同专家援助战略的有效性,结果见表5。 与主要文件中关于`0\pi_{0}-FAST ' 的结论一致,R2-VLA实现了最高的平均任务成功率,同时需要的专家援助远远少于基于不确定性的替代战略。 具体地说,在微型VLA中,R2-VLA的平均成功率为62.8%,ASK率仅为20.8%,成绩优于DINO距离(58.5%成功,ASK为34.0%)和Action Entropy(58.8%成功,ASK为34.0%)。 同样,在OpenVLA中,R2-VLA取得了68.6%的成功,其中33.3%为ASK,而DINO距离则取得了66.8%的成功,51.4%为ASK,成功率67.3%为Ask for Action Entropy。 这些结果表明,所学到的不确定性确定了更多的决策点,使得R2-VLA能够在专家援助较少的情况下取得更高的任务成功.

blocks.en: Furthermore, when compared with Random ASK under matched ASK budgets, R2-VLA improves average success by 7.9 percentage points on MiniVLA (62.8% versus 54.9%) and 8.3 percentage points on OpenVLA (68.6% versus 60.3%). This indicates that the improvements cannot be attributed solely to the additional expert actions, but rather to the ability of the learned uncertainty to identify when autonomous execution is uncertain. Together with the π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST results in the main paper, these findings demonstrate that R2-VLA consistently improves task success while reducing the frequency of expert assistance across different VLA architectures and model scales.

blocks.en: We investigate how different user-specified risk levels ϵ \epsilon affect the performance of R2-VLA. Specifically, we vary the target success rate 1 − ϵ 1-\epsilon and independently calibrate the corresponding threshold λ ^ \hat{\lambda} . Figure 3 illustrates the resulting trade-offs between task success and ASK rate for π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST, MiniVLA, and OpenVLA, respectively, across all four LIBERO suites. As the target success rate increases, R2-VLA generally requests more expert assistance, leading to improved task success. Importantly, the observed success rates closely track or exceed the prescribed targets across different risk levels, demonstrating that R2-VLA can adapt its ACT/ASK decisions to varying task success requirements. The results also reveal differences across task suites: LIBERO- Long generally requires more frequent expert assistance to achieve a given success rate, reflecting the greater difficulty of long-horizon manipulation tasks. blocks.en: We evaluate the contribution of corrupted retrieval contexts during uncertainty-head training by comparing R2-VLA against a variant trained exclusively with clean retrieval demonstrations. As shown in Table 6 , incorporating retrieval corruption consistently improves average task success while substantially reducing ASK rate across all three VLA backbones. Specifically, for MiniVLA, the average success rate increases from 59.5% to 62.8%, while the ASK rate decreases from 33.9% to 20.8%. Similar improvements are observed for π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST, where the success rate increases from 70.5% to 72.0% and the ASK rate decreases from 61.7% to 49.0%, and for OpenVLA, where the success rate increases from 67.2% to 68.6% while the ASK rate decreases from 47.4% to 33.3%. These results suggest that exposing the uncertainty head to misleading retrieval contexts improves its ability to distinguish certain from uncertain retrieval-guided actions. Importantly, the reduction in ASK rate is accompanied by improved task success, indicating that retrieval corruption does not merely encourage more conservative uncertainty estimates but instead enables more selective expert assistance. Overall, these findings support the importance of explicitly incorporating retrieval failure modes into uncertainty-head training to improve both task success rate and expert assitance frequency.
blocks.zh: 我们通过将R2-VLA与专门经过清洁检索演示培训的变体相比较,来评价在不确定源培训期间腐败的检索环境的贡献。 如表6所示,纳入追回腐败的做法不断提高平均任务成功率,同时大幅降低所有三个职业劳工协会骨干部门ASK的比率。 具体地说,在MiniVLA中,平均成功率从59.5%上升到62.8%,而ASK则从33.9%下降到20.8%。 0\\pi\0}-FAST也有类似的改进,成功率从70.5%上升到72.0%,ASK从61.7%下降到49.0%,OpenVLA的成功率从67.2%上升到68.6%,而ASK从47.4%下降到33.3%。 这些结果表明,将不确定性置于误导性检索背景下,可提高它区分某些和不确定的检索指导行动的能力。 重要的是,在降低ASK比率的同时,任务的成功也有所改善,这表明追回腐败不仅鼓励更保守的不确定性估计,反而促成更有选择的专家援助。 总的来说,这些结论支持将检索失败模式明确纳入不确定源培训以提高任务成功率和专家犹豫频率的重要性。

blocks.en: We investigate the sensitivity of R2-VLA to the number of calibration episodes N cal N_{\mathrm{cal}} . Specifically, we vary N cal ∈ { 50,100,200,400 } N_{\mathrm{cal}}\in\{50,100,200,400\} while keeping the other parameter fixed. As shown in Table 7 , increasing the calibration-set size consistently reduces the frequency of expert assistance while maintaining relatively stable task success across all four LIBERO suites. In particular, increasing N cal N_{\mathrm{cal}} from 50 50 to 400 400 reduces the average ASK rate from 55.1 % 55.1\% to 45.9 % 45.9\% , while the average success rate remains around 72 % 72\% . This suggests that additional calibration data improves the ability of the risk-control procedure to identify thresholds that permit more autonomous execution without substantially compromising task success. Notably, the default setting of N cal = 200 N_{\mathrm{cal}}=200 , used in our main experiments, already achieves a favorable trade-off between task success and expert assistance, with an average success rate of 72.0 % 72.0\% and an ASK rate of 49.0 % 49.0\% . These findings demonstrate that R2-VLA can maintain relatively stable task performance across different calibration-set sizes while reducing unnecessary expert assistance as more calibration data becomes available.
